initial.prompt:
<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.

### Common mistakes to avoid:

**Mistake 1: Bare comma-separated atoms without a head.**
```
WRONG:  input(BR, BC, V), V != 0.
RIGHT:  nonzero(BR, BC, V) :- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0.
```

**Mistake 2: Assignment without a head predicate.**
```
WRONG:  offset1 = BR + BC.
RIGHT:  offset1(O) :- O = BR + BC, input(BR, BC, _).
```

**Mistake 3: Putting aggregate on the left of `=`.**
```
WRONG:  #min{R : input(R,_,_)} = Rmin.
RIGHT:  Rmin = #min{R : input(R,_,_)}.
```

**Mistake 4: Unsafe variables (variables not grounded in a positive predicate).**
```
WRONG:  col_nonzero(C) :- #count{R : input(R,C,V), V != 0} > 0.
RIGHT:  col_nonzero(C) :- input(_, C, _), #count{R : input(R,C,V), V != 0} > 0.
```

**Mistake 5: Using `#mod` instead of `\`.**
```
WRONG:  even(C) :- C #mod 2 = 0.
RIGHT:  even(C) :- C \ 2 = 0.
```

**Mistake 6: Using `aggregate/3` (SWI-Prolog syntax).**
```
WRONG:  row_five_count(R, N) :- aggregate(N = #count, input(R,_,5), N).
RIGHT:  row_five_count(R, N) :- N = #count{C : input(R,C,5)}.
```

Use `#show output/3.` at the end of your program so Clingo only prints the output predicate.
</rules>

Below is one worked example, followed by a reusable template.

<example_1>
This puzzle copies all non-zero cells from input to output and removes cells with color 0.

<example_grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</example_grid_1>

<example_grid_2>
Input:
<diagram>
0 0 0
0 0 5
0 0 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 0 0
0 0 5
0 0 0
</diagram>
</example_grid_2>

<transformation>
The output is identical to the input: every cell keeps its original color.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).
</asp>
</example_1>

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.

% Rows and columns with at least one non-zero
row_has_nonzero(R) :- input(R, C, Color), Color != 0.
col_has_nonzero(C) :- input(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Bounding box
min_row(M) :- M = #min{R : row_has_nonzero(R)}.
max_row(M) :- M = #max{R : row_has_nonzero(R)}.
min_col(M) :- M = #min{C : col_has_nonzero(C)}.
max_col(M) :- M = #max{C : col_has_nonzero(C)}.

% Border color (top‑left corner)
border_color(B) :- input(min_row, min_col, B), B != 0.

% Corners must share the same border color
:- input(min_row, max_col, C), C != 0, C != border_color.
:- input(max_row, min_col, D), D != 0, D != border_color.
:- input(max_row, max_col, E), E != 0, E != border_color.
:- border_color != 0.

% Output dimensions (interior of the bounding rectangle)
inter_rows(IR) :- IR = max_row - min_row - 1.
inter_cols(JC) :- JC = max_col - min_col - 1.

% Interior cells (mapped to output indices I,J)
interior_cell(I,J,R,C,Color) :- 
    I = 0..IR-1,
    J = 0..JC-1,
    input(R,C,Color),
    R = min_row + 1 + I,
    C = min_col + 1 + J.

interior_cell(I,J,R,C,Color) :- interior_cell(I,J,R,C,Color).

interior_cell(I,J,R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,Color), R = min_row + 1 + I, C = min_col + 1 + J.

% Interior cells that have a non‑zero (will be recolored)
interior_nonzero(I,J,B) :-

    Color != 0,
    B = border_color.

% Interior cells that are zero (will stay zero)
interior_zero(I,J) :- 
    interior_cell(I,J,R,C,Color),
    Color == 0.

% Output cell for each interior position
output_cell(I,J) :- interior_cell(I,J,R,C,Color).

% Exactly one colour for each output cell (will be forced by constraints)
1 { output(I,J,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(I,J).

% For non‑zero interior cells output must use the border colour

% For zero interior cells output must be zero
:- interior_zero(I,J), output(I,J,Color), Color != 0.

full_program:
asp
% Bounding rectangle of non‑zero cells
min_row(N)  :- N = #min{R : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
max_row(N)  :- N = #max{R : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
min_col(N)  :- N = #min{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
max_col(N)  :- N = #max{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.

% Colour of the outer frame – colour of the top‑left non‑zero cell
outer_color(C) :- input(min_row, min_col, C), C != 0.

% Size of the interior (remove one layer on each side)
inter_rows(N) :- N = max_row - min_row - 1, N > 0.
inter_cols(M) :- M = max_col - min_col - 1, M > 0.

% Enumerate interior rows (safe – I is grounded)
inter_row(I,R) :- I = 0..inter_rows(N), R = min_row + 1 + I.

% Enumerate interior columns (safe – J is grounded)
inter_col(J,C) :- J = 0..inter_cols(M), C = min_col + 1 + J.

% Original colour of the interior cell at (I,J)
inter_cell(I,J,R,C,Col) :-
    inter_row(I,R),
    inter_col(J,C),
    input(R, C, Col).

% Output cell – copy interior cells:
%   • non‑zero interior cells become the outer colour,
%   • zero interior cells stay zero.
output(I,J,Col) :-
    inter_cell(I,J,R,C,Col),
    Col != 0,
    outer_color(Col).

output(I,J,0) :-
    inter_cell(I,J,R,C,0).

% Exactly one colour for each interior position
1 { output(I,J,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output(I,J,Color).

#show output/3.

% Dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Bounding rectangle of non-zero cells
row_has_nonzero(R) :- input(R, C, Color), Color != 0.
col_has_nonzero(C) :- input(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Minimal and maximal rows and columns with non-zero cells
min_row(M) :- M = #min{R : row_has_nonzero(R)}.
max_row(M) :- M = #max{R : row_has_nonzero(R)}.
min_col(M) :- M = #min{C : col_has_nonzero(C)}.
max_col(M) :- M = #max{C : col_has_nonzero(C)}.

% Border color: color of the top-left corner (must be non-zero)
border_color(B) :- input(min_row, min_col, B), B != 0.

% Compute interior dimensions (remove one outer layer on each side)
inter_rows(IR) :- IR = max_row - min_row - 1.
inter_cols(JC) :- JC = max_col - min_col - 1.

% Interior cells mapping to output coordinates
interior_cell(I,J,R,C,OrigColor) :-
    I = 0..IR-1,
    J = 0..JC-1,
    input(R,C,OrigColor),
    R = min_row + 1 + I,
    C = min_col + 1 + J.

% Output cell for each interior position
output_cell(I,J,R,C,OrigColor) :- interior_cell(I,J,R,C,OrigColor).

% Exactly one color per output cell
1 { output(I,J,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(I,J,R,C,OrigColor).

% Enforce correct color: non-zero original becomes border_color, zero stays 0
:- output(I,J,Color), interior_cell(I,J,R,C,OrigColor), OrigColor != 0, Color != border_color.
:- output(I,J,Color), interior_cell(I,J,R,C,OrigColor), OrigColor == 0, Color = 0.

% Bounding rectangle of non‑zero cells
min_row(N) :- N = #min{R : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
max_row(N) :- N = #max{R : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
min_col(N) :- N = #min{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
max_col(N) :- N = #max{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.

% Colour of the outer frame
outer_color(C) :- input(min_row, min_col, C), C != 0.

% Size of interior (remove one layer on each side)
inter_rows_count(N) :- N = max_row - min_row - 1, N > 0.
inter_cols_count(M) :- M = max_col - min_col - 1, M > 0.

% Enumerate interior rows
inter_row(I,R) :- I = 0..inter_rows_count(N), R = min_row + 1 + I.

% Enumerate interior columns
inter_col(J,C) :- J = 0..inter_cols_count(M), C = min_col + 1 + J.

% Original colour of interior cell
inter_cell(I,J,R,C,Color) :-
    inter_row(I,R),
    inter_col(J,C),
    input(R, C, Color).

% Output cell – non‑zero interior cells become outer colour,
% zero interior cells stay zero.
output(I,J,Color) :-
    inter_cell(I,J,R,C,Color),
    Color != 0,
    outer_color(Color).

output(I,J,0) :-

% Bounding rectangle of non‑zero cells
min_row(N)  :- N = #min{R : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
max_row(N)  :- N = #max{R : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
min_col(N)  :- N = #min{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.
max_col(N)  :- N = #max{C : input(R, C, Color), Color != 0}.

% Colour of the outer frame – colour of the top‑left non‑zero cell
outer_color(C) :- input(min_row, min_col, C), C != 0.

% Size of the interior (remove one layer on each side)
inter_rows(N) :- N = max_row - min_row - 1, N > 0.
inter_cols(M) :- M = max_col - min_col - 1, M > 0.

% Enumerate interior rows (safe – I is grounded)
inter_row(I,R) :- I = 0..inter_rows(N), R = min_row + 1 + I.

% Enumerate interior columns (safe – J is grounded)
inter_col(J,C) :- J = 0..inter_cols(M), C = min_col + 1 + J.

% Original colour of the interior cell at (I,J)
inter_cell(I,J,R,C,Col) :-
    inter_row(I,R),
    inter_col(J,C),
    input(R, C, Col).

% Output cell – copy interior cells:
%   • non‑zero interior cells become the outer colour,
%   • zero interior cells stay zero.
output(I,J,Col) :-
    inter_cell(I,J,R,C,Col),
    Col != 0,
    outer_color(Col).

output(I,J,0) :-
    inter_cell(I,J,R,C,0).

% Exactly one colour for each interior position
1 { output(I,J,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output(I,J,Color).
